expected_outcome: The intended current page role is explicit for the accepted user task and downstream routing uses that role.
baseline_evidence: Accepted upstream ownership/architecture evidence plus current role correction.
minimum_verification: Re-read current affected pages and verify the final role/routing artifact after implementation.
optional_first_party_metric: When authorized/available, use query-to-URL Webmaster evidence to see whether the intended page is associated with the relevant query family.
review_trigger: After implementation and search reprocessing, or immediately if the page is materially repurposed/removed.
failure_policy: If page roles remain ambiguous or new overlap appears, reopen only the affected ownership/architecture boundary.
claim_boundary: Role correctness can be checked without promising ranking, traffic, leads or revenue.

expected_outcome: Each overlapping page has a distinct documented responsibility; no destructive consolidation is implied unless separately authorized.
baseline_evidence: Current overlap/delta evidence and accepted frozen owner.
minimum_verification: Re-read both pages after differentiation and verify scope, internal handoff and no accidental duplicated primary responsibility.
optional_first_party_metric: If later authorized/available, inspect query-by-URL history to test whether ownership is fragmented or alternating.
review_trigger: After implementation/search reprocessing or when one page materially changes scope.
failure_policy: If differentiation is not visible or evidence suggests harmful competition, reopen the affected pair in the dedicated conflict-diagnosis method.
claim_boundary: Current overlap is not proof of historical competition or harm.

expected_outcome: The explicit previously missing user need is visibly and truthfully served on the accepted existing owner.
baseline_evidence: Current-page read plus explicit missing-needs evidence.
minimum_verification: Re-read the page and test every named missing need against the implemented content.
optional_first_party_metric: If available, track relevant query impressions/clicks/CTR/position and configured Metrika goals as supporting outcome evidence.
review_trigger: After publication and an appropriate search-observation window; also when offer/content truth changes.
failure_policy: If the named need remains uncovered or implementation changes the page task, correct the content or reopen the affected owner decision.
claim_boundary: Content completion is verifiable; ranking/conversion uplift is not guaranteed.

expected_outcome: Current-page recheck either confirms a material within-owner content gap and it is improved, or closes the candidate as no-change.
baseline_evidence: Bounded exact-query AI evidence plus direct current target/source evidence from the accepted comparison step.
minimum_verification: Direct current target read against the exact candidate dimensions.
optional_first_party_metric: A later AI/search recheck is optional only when it has explicit information gain and authorization.
review_trigger: When the current target materially changes or a later authorized AI observation is collected.
failure_policy: Do not create architecture change from a single snapshot; preserve NO_CHANGE/INSUFFICIENT when evidence does not support the candidate.
claim_boundary: This is not sitewide AI visibility or longitudinal stability measurement.

expected_outcome: The exact approved source-to-target link exists in a useful current source context and points to the accepted target.
baseline_evidence: Accepted link recommendation and previous as-is topology state.
minimum_verification: Fetch/read source HTML and verify a normalized literal a-href edge plus source context and target-task fit.
optional_first_party_metric: None required for implementation acceptance; performance analytics may be reviewed later if in scope.
review_trigger: Immediately after implementation and after material source/target redesign.
failure_policy: Missing/wrong/contextless edge returns to NOT_IMPLEMENTED or DEFER; do not infer implementation from endpoint liveness.
claim_boundary: Implemented link does not guarantee rankings or traffic.

expected_outcome: The exact user task is consistently assigned to the accepted current page/supporting path without creating an unnecessary new URL.
baseline_evidence: Final structural-unit and target authority from accepted Step12/14/14A artifacts.
minimum_verification: Verify final phrase/unit-to-target mapping and current target role; implementation mechanics are calibrated with the actual site owner/CMS.
optional_first_party_metric: When available, query-to-URL evidence can support later validation of actual search association.
review_trigger: After implementation or if the target page/role changes.
failure_policy: If the target no longer fits, reopen the affected route only; never manufacture a new page from missing implementation detail.
claim_boundary: Analytical routing is not proof that a CMS change or link has been implemented.

expected_outcome: No implementation action occurs until the exact blocker is resolved.
baseline_evidence: HOLD ledger blocker class, reason and recheck trigger.
minimum_verification: Obtain the named missing business truth, policy, clarified task, or authoritative evidence; then re-enter prioritization for that item.
optional_first_party_metric: Not applicable until the blocker is resolved.
failure_policy: Keep HOLD; do not downgrade as low value and do not invent implementation effort/priority.
claim_boundary: HOLD means unresolved, not rejected and not low-value.
